name: Wormian Bone Multiple Fractures Dentinogenesis Imperfecta Skeletal Dysplasia
aliases: Wormian Bone Syndrome with Multiple Fractures and Dentinogenesis Imperfecta
Skeletal Dysplasia with Wormian Bones and Dentinogenesis Imperfecta

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Wormian Bone Multiple Fractures Dentinogenesis Imperfecta Skeletal Dysplasia

criteria.description: Presence of multiple wormian bones identified on skull radiographs
Recurrent multiple bone fractures with minimal trauma
Clinical and radiographic evidence of dentinogenesis imperfecta affecting primary and permanent teeth
Radiological evidence of skeletal dysplasia including bone deformities and growth abnormalities
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: wormian bones, multiple fractures, and dentinogenesis imperfecta
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

laboratory: Normal serum calcium and phosphate levels
imaging: Multiple wormian bones on skull X-rays
Radiographic evidence of multiple fractures and bone deformities
Dental radiographs showing bulbous crowns and obliterated pulp chambers
genetic: Mutations in genes associated with collagen synthesis and dentinogenesis (e.g., COL1A1, DSPP) may be identified
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Clinical dental examination revealing opalescent teeth

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of dentinogenesis imperfecta in some types
Genetic mutations primarily in COL1A1 and COL1A2
Early loss of teeth without root resorption
Metabolic bone disease with different biochemical profile

redFlags: Multiple low-trauma fractures in infancy or early childhood
Severe dentinogenesis imperfecta leading to early tooth loss
Progressive skeletal deformities causing functional impairment
specialistType: Dentist specialized in genetic dental disorders
